stories.headline: Yemen's Houthis strike Saudi energy facilities as US hits Iranian oil tankers
stories.body:
Yemen's Houthis launched drone and missile attacks against four southern Saudi cities on Tuesday [c1]. The strikes set oil installations on fire [c1]. They also wounded dozens of people [c1]. Saudi authorities said 73 people were hurt across southern Saudi Arabia [c2]. Women and children were among those injured [c2]. Fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen is raising fears of full-scale war [c17].

United States forces struck multiple Iranian oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [c3]. US officials said the strikes followed Iranian attempts to hit a US Navy warship [c3]. US officials told CNN that strikes targeted tankers near Kharg Island on Tuesday [c8]. Iranian state media said a US missile hit an Iranian tanker 6km from Kharg Island [c4]. State media said another tanker was attacked near Jask on the Gulf of Oman [c4].

Iranian Armed Forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi issued a warning [c10]. Abdollahi said any attack on Iranian tankers would trigger strikes against US bases [c10]. He said these strikes would hit US bases across the region [c10]. The Revolutionary Guard warned crews on oil tankers in Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports to leave immediately [c5]. The Guard threatened to target those vessels [c5]. International benchmark Brent crude briefly reached $99.46 a barrel on Tuesday as tensions in the Gulf rose [c12].

The United States government announced new aviation sanctions against Iran [c6]. The Trump administration put sanctions on 27 Iranian airlines [c9]. It also targeted nine service providers accused of supporting Mahan Air [c9]. The Treasury designed these rules to ground Iranian airlines [c6].

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it captured a US submersible near the Strait of Hormuz [c7]. A US official said a defective underwater military drone had malfunctioned [c7]. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins said an older-model surveillance drone submersible malfunctioned in regional waters [c15]. Hawkins said it contained no sensitive data [c15]. He said it had no classified radar equipment [c15]. The Revolutionary Guard also claimed it destroyed an MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz [c11]. It said it used a new Iranian air defence system [c11].

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Oman reached significant progress [c13]. He said the talks focused on managing the Strait of Hormuz [c13]. The broader conflict has claimed the lives of 18 US service members [c16]. Related violence occurred elsewhere in the region [c14]. Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon killed 13 people on Monday [c14]. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported that death toll [c14].

vocab.meaning: a small craft designed to operate underwater
penalties imposed by one country on another to change its behavior

stories.headline: Britain, France, and Canada ban imports from West Bank settlements
stories.body:
Britain, France, and Canada announced trade restrictions blocking imports from Israeli West Bank settlements [c27]. Twelve countries acted together or considered measures against trade with settlements in the West Bank [c18]. The UK government banned goods from Israeli settlements there [c20]. It restricted services to settlements [c20]. It also put limits on arms sales that contribute to the occupation [c20]. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said settler terrorism in parts of the West Bank amounted to ethnic cleansing [c21]. He said the Israeli government turned a blind eye [c21]. Palestinian ambassador Dr Husam Zomlot called the trade decision a turning point [c22]. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said targeted measures were brought forward to support a two-state solution [c25]. Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch criticized the decision and accused the Labour government of antisemitism [c26].

France cited the expansion of settlements and violence as its reason for banning goods [c29]. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said illegal settlements undermine long-term peace objectives [c28]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington will not follow these bans [c30].

Israel ordered the closure of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem [c19, c23]. Israel also removed British representatives from the International Gaza Support Centre [c19]. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced entry bans on 12 Britons [c24]. Israel announced plans for 1,000 new West Bank homes on Tuesday [c31].

vocab.meaning: a diplomatic office of one government located in a foreign city
official limits placed on choices or actions

stories.headline: Canada places counter-tariffs on $20 billion of US goods
stories.body:
Canada put counter-tariffs on roughly 20 billion dollars of American goods on Tuesday [c37, c40]. The Canadian tariffs range from 15% to 50% [c37, c40]. They target nearly 28 billion Canadian dollars worth of goods [c37]. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the trade shift away from the US will cost money [c36]. Carney said it is necessary to protect Canadian workers [c36]. He said Canada is the largest customer for US goods in 26 states [c35].

The US maintains a 25% tariff on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium, and lumber [c38]. It put 50% tariffs in late August on Canadian dairy, alcohol, hockey sticks, and perfume [c38]. Canada lost about 41,000 jobs in August after trade talks collapsed [c39]. Donald Trump threatened to block Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier from selling in the US [c33]. Trump wants Bombardier to move manufacturing to the United States [c33]. Bombardier employs over 3,000 people in the US [c34].

The Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor opened recently [c41]. US officials did not attend the opening event [c41]. US consumers faced record average new car prices over $52,000 in September [c43].

vocab.meaning: taxes imposed by a country in response to taxes set by another nation
the business of making products in large numbers in factories

stories.headline: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin hold hour-long phone call on Ukraine
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump held an hour-long phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday [c44]. Trump said he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine [c44]. The call followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner [c45]. The envoys met Putin in Moscow on Saturday for over three hours [c50]. They then traveled to Kyiv on Sunday [c50].

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the call as constructive and frank [c47]. Ushakov said Putin told Trump that Russia has no aggressive plans towards European states [c46]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Trump for sending the envoys [c48]. Zelenskyy said peace ideas presented by Kushner included a couple of very good ideas [c52]. But Zelenskyy said he did not see a quick end to the conflict [c51]. Zelenskyy expressed hope to meet Trump around September 20 at the UN General Assembly [c53].

Russian strikes killed at least five civilians in Kyiv on Tuesday morning [c49]. Ukrainian attacks caused casualties in Bryansk, Kursk, and Crimea [c49]. The European Commission approved a 3.7 billion dollar loan for Kyiv to buy Patriot parts [c55].

vocab.meaning: representatives sent by a government on a official mission
helpful and serving a useful purpose

stories.headline: Delhi authorities order building audits after seven die in housing collapse
stories.body:
Delhi authorities ordered building audits after seven people died in a five-storey house collapse on Sunday [c58, c70]. The building housed a boys' paying guest accommodation in Satya Niketan [c58]. It was undergoing basement repairs and ground-floor renovation work when it collapsed [c62]. Delhi Police arrested property owner Urmila Gupta, her husband Hariram, and their son Mahesh [c60]. They face charges of culpable homicide and negligence [c60]. Police also apprehended labour contractor Sanoj in Uttar Pradesh [c61].

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi demolished 24 properties across Delhi after the collapse [c68]. It also sealed seven illegal structures [c68]. The MCD suspended South Zone deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar and four engineers [c69]. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta instructed officials to demolish an adjacent dilapidated building [c67]. Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu ordered a structural audit of all student housing hubs within a week [c70].

A Supreme Court bench agreed to examine student housing collapses across India [c63]. The Delhi High Court directed the MCD to inspect all paying guest accommodations [c72]. It criticized authorities for failing to build enough hostels [c71].

vocab.meaning: the killing of one human being by another
falling apart or in a state of ruin

stories.headline: Prime Minister Modi calls for global expansion of UPI at Fintech Fest
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the seventh edition of the Global Fintech Fest [c73]. During his speech, Modi urged the fintech ecosystem to expand the global reach of UPI [c73]. UPI is a real-time payment system developed in India [c75]. Real-time payment transactions using UPI reached 24.51 billion as of August [c75].

The UPI platform is expanding across international borders [c76]. It is currently live in 11 countries [c76]. In addition, the platform is linked directly with Singapore's local payment system [c76]. Modi asked financial technology companies to take the system into even more nations [c73].

Modi also urged the fintech industry to look beyond payments [c77]. He asked firms to focus heavily on non-payment transactions [c77]. Specifically, he called for wider access to savings products [c77]. He urged companies to expand access to pensions [c77]. He also encouraged them to provide better access to insurance [c77].

Modi spoke about the strength of the national economy [c74]. He said India's economy achieved 7.8 per cent real GDP growth in the June quarter [c74]. He stressed that the country hit this growth rate despite challenges [c74]. Those economic challenges came from the ongoing conflict in West Asia [c74].

Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra also addressed the Global Fintech Fest [c79]. Malhotra said Indian fintech firms have reshaped finance [c79]. He said these companies succeeded by taking banking directly into the hands of every citizen [c79].

The country received positive news regarding its economic rating [c78]. Japan Credit Rating Agency upgraded India's sovereign credit rating [c78]. It raised the rating to 'A-' from 'BBB+' [c78]. This move was the agency's first upgrade for India in three decades [c78].

vocab.meaning: formally introduced or opened an event
relating to a national government and its independent status
